newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: World Bank pays first visit to Belgrade in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: World Bank pays first visit to Belgrade in 5 yrs.

text.p: Yugoslavia can hope for new World Bank financial support only after it clears its debt to the institution and settles membership of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), a World Bank economist said on Tuesday.

"Yugoslavia must first return to international financial institutions, regain membership in the IMF and settle large amounts of arrears before any new lending will be available," Ilham Zuryk, chief of the first World Bank mission to arrive in Belgrade in five years, told Reuters.
According to Zuryk, arrears exceeded $1 billion.
"The purpose of our visit is to present our study "From Plan To Market' but also to update our knowledge of the situation in Yugoslavia," she said.
"This updating mission is currently held to explore all relevant data from both official and unofficial sources," said another World Bank economist, John Nellis.
The five-member mission held further closed-door contacts with Yugoslav government representatives and monetary authorities.
World Bank officials made their first public appearance here on Tuesday, presenting the Bank's 1996 World Development Report.
"Over the years, the Bank has learned the value of sharing experience with the public in member countries," said Zuryk, introducing the report.
Alan Gelb and John Nellis pointed to some common problems shared by countries in transition and stressed the need for restructuring legal, financial and government institutions.

Economists said their report dealt with liberalisation, property rights, privatisation, how to build institutions adapted to the market economy and the social conseqences of transition. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
